summary.text: Tracey Schroeder is the Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 46 in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing incumbent Jesse Gabriel (D).
A teacher with the Los Angeles Unified School District since 1998, she also ran for the seat in 2024.

paragraphs.text: Tracey Schroeder was born in Los Angeles, California, and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of California, Los Angeles in 1996 and a graduate degree from the Phillips Graduate Institute in 2006.
Her career experience includes working as a teacher for LAUSD beginning in 1998, and she has been a volunteer teacher abroad and a volunteer with several service organizations.
Schroeder received 26.3 percent in the 2022 nonpartisan primary for Los Angeles Unified School District Board of Education District 4, finishing behind incumbent Nick Melvoin.
In 2024 she advanced from the March primary to the general election for Assembly District 46, where incumbent Jesse Gabriel defeated her, 62.9 percent to 37.1 percent.
In the June 2, 2026 primary she again advanced alongside Gabriel, receiving 33.8 percent of the vote.

In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, Schroeder listed her campaign priorities as public safety, including support for Proposition 36 and repeal of Proposition 47; improving the economy through lower taxes and regulations; accountable, results-based help for the homeless; and education, including audits of education spending and respect for parents' rights.
